stem: What is an array?

options.content: A fixed number of items of one type under one name
A structure that groups fields of different data types
A variable that can hold only one value at a time
A list that grows as items are added

explanation: An array has a fixed size and one data type.

stem: What is the index of an array element?

options.content: The number that gives its position
The value stored in the element
options.rationale: That is the content of the element.

options.content: The data type shared by all the elements of the array
options.rationale: All the elements share the type.

options.content: The number of elements that the array can hold in all
options.rationale: That is the size of the array.

explanation: An index selects an element.

stem: An array is declared `DECLARE Temps : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER` and holds 18, 21, 19, 25, 23. What is the value of `Temps[4]`?

options.rationale: That is the index, not the value.

stem: An array is declared `ARRAY[1:30] OF STRING`. Which statement causes an error?

Correct: 31 is outside the bounds 1 to 30.
Index 30 is the upper bound and is valid.

stem: Which data is best stored in a two-dimensional array?

options.content: The names of all the pupils who are in a class
options.rationale: A list of names needs one index.

options.content: The total mark that is scored by a single pupil
options.rationale: A single value needs no array.

options.content: Takings of five shops on each of seven days
options.rationale: Correct: each value needs a shop and a day.

explanation: A table with two characteristics suits two indexes.
hints: Which data forms a table of rows and columns?

stem: Which is a feature of a static data structure such as an array?

options.content: It can grow while the program runs
Its elements may have different types
Its size is fixed when it is declared
It uses memory only for the items stored
options.rationale: Memory is reserved for the whole array.

explanation: A static structure cannot change size while the program runs.
hints: Can an array be made bigger by the program?

stem: A Python list `scores` holds the marks of eight pupils. Which expression gives the mark of the fourth pupil?

options.rationale: Round brackets are for function calls.

stem: A 2D array `Seats` is declared `ARRAY[1:6, 1:5] OF BOOLEAN`. Which statement is true?

options.rationale: The columns only go up to 5.

explanation: Row first, column second, within 1 to 6 and 1 to 5.

stem: All the elements of an array must have the same data type.
explanation: True. That is why a record is used when the items have different types.

stem: A two-dimensional array needs a single loop to process every element.
explanation: False. It normally needs nested loops, one for the rows and one for the columns.

stem: Match each term to its meaning.

right.content: Its size is fixed when it is declared
Each element is identified by a row and a column
One item stored in an array
The number that identifies an element's position

explanation: Terms used with arrays.

stem: Complete the pseudocode that adds up the seven values of the array `Rain`.

payload.template:
DECLARE Rain : ARRAY[1:{{blank:a}}] OF INTEGER

Total ← 0

FOR Day ← 1 TO {{blank:b}}

Total ← Total + Rain[{{blank:c}}]

NEXT Day

explanation: Seven elements, a loop from 1 to 7 and the loop variable as the index.
hints: Declare the bounds as [1:n] and use a counter loop to visit each element.

stem: Explain why an array is better than 30 separate variables for storing the marks of a class. [3]

points.description: One identifier holds all the marks and an index selects one
A loop can process all the elements, so the code is short
The program can be changed for a different class size by changing the bounds

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: One identifier holds all 30 marks and the index chooses one. A loop can process every element, so the code is short, and the size can be changed easily.

explanation: One name, an index and loops.
hints: Think about the code needed for 30 pupils with and without an array.

stem: The array `Marks` holds 10 integers (indexes 1 to 10). Write pseudocode to calculate and output their average. [4]

points.description: Total set to 0 before the loop
A loop from 1 to 10 using the loop variable as the index
Adds Marks[Index] to the total inside the loop
Divides the total by 10 after the loop and outputs the result

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
Total ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 10
    Total ← Total + Marks[Index]
NEXT Index
Average ← Total / 10
OUTPUT Average
```

explanation: A running total then a division.
hints: Total, then divide by 10; the loop runs 10 times.

stem: Write pseudocode to find and output the largest value in the array `Data`, which has indexes 1 to 20. [4]

points.description: Sets Largest to Data[1] before the loop
A loop through the other elements (2 to 20) using the index
Compares Data[Index] with Largest and replaces Largest when it is bigger
Outputs Largest after the loop

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
Largest ← Data[1]
FOR Index ← 2 TO 20
    IF Data[Index] > Largest THEN
        Largest ← Data[Index]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Largest
```

explanation: Compare each element with the largest so far.
hints: Start with the first element as the largest.

stem: Give two advantages and one disadvantage of an array as a static data structure. [3]

points.description: Advantage: access to any element is quick because its position is worked out from the index
Advantage: the elements are stored together and the memory needed is known in advance
Disadvantage: the size is fixed, so memory is wasted if it is too large and items cannot be added if it is too small

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Any element can be reached quickly from its index, and the memory needed is known in advance. The size is fixed, so memory is wasted if the array is too big and items cannot be added if it is too small.

explanation: Fast access against fixed size.
hints: Consider memory and speed of access.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which is the correct declaration of the array?

options.rationale: This is not the pseudocode form.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the total rainfall for the week.

parts.label: (c)

parts.workedSolution: The largest of the seven values is 25.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State the index of the largest value.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Write pseudocode that outputs the number of days on which the rainfall was more than 10 mm.

points.description: A counter set to 0 before the loop
A loop from 1 to 7 testing Rain[Index] > 10
Adds 1 to the counter inside the IF and outputs it after the loop

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
Wet ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 7
    IF Rain[Index] > 10 THEN
        Wet ← Wet + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Wet
```

parts.stem: Explain why an array is used rather than seven separate variables.

points.description: The elements can be processed with a loop using the index

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A loop can process the elements using the index, so the code is shorter and easier to change than with seven variables.

parts.explanation: An index lets a loop do the repeating.

hints: Total, largest and a counter are all found in one pass.

stem:
A company stores the weekly sales of three shops in the two-dimensional array `Sales`, declared `ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF INTEGER`. The rows are the shops and the columns are the weeks.

|  | Week 1 | Week 2 | Week 3 | Week 4 |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Shop 1 | 120 | 95 | 140 | 110 |
| Shop 2 | 80 | 105 | 90 | 125 |
| Shop 3 | 150 | 130 | 115 | 160 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the total sales of Shop 3 over the four weeks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the total sales of all three shops in Week 3.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Write pseudocode using nested loops that outputs the total of all the values in the array.

points.description: Total set to 0 before the loops
An outer loop for the rows (1 to 3) and an inner loop for the columns (1 to 4)
Adds Sales[Row, Col] to the total and outputs the total after the loops

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
Total ← 0
FOR Row ← 1 TO 3
    FOR Col ← 1 TO 4
        Total ← Total + Sales[Row, Col]
    NEXT Col
NEXT Row
OUTPUT Total
```

parts.explanation: Nested loops visit every cell; the answer is 1 420.

explanation: Reading and processing a 2D array of sales.
hints: The first index is the shop (row).
A column total adds the three shops for one week.
